decision.title: The tree-sitter functions are tree-sitter:parse and tree-sitter:languages (packet )
decision.summary: The tree-sitter functions are tree-sitter:parse and tree-sitter:languages in urn:sxml:tree-sitter, replacing sxml:parse-code and sxml:code-languages, while the sxml:token and sxml:node elements stay in urn:sxml.

body.p: , after , , , , , , , . The owner (2026-10-22): "expose tree-sitter as tree-sitter: not sxml:code-". Amends 's *API** paragraph; the shape of the documents ('s Shape) is unchanged.

item.p: Whom it serves: users who write queries and stylesheets; the name says what the functions are (tree-sitter's parser), as bin: and file: do for EXPath's modules.

Names: tree-sitter:parse($source as xs:string?, $language as xs:string, $options as map(*)? := {}) as document-node()? and tree-sitter:languages() as xs:string*, with the signatures, options (highlights, positions, injections) and results of sxml:parse-code and sxml:code-languages, which are removed (no aliases).

Namespace ( default): urn:sxml:tree-sitter, conventional prefix tree-sitter. tree-sitter defines no XML namespace of its own, and a URI under its domain would claim a name its project never published; sxml's other URNs are already urn:sxml:... (urn:sxml:timezone-data:, urn:sxml:default). name.h (frozen, additive after , as and ): SXML_NAMESPACE_TREE_SITTER = 17 after SXML_NAMESPACE_SXML, SXML_NAMESPACE_WELL_KNOWN_COUNT 18; no value changes. The comment of SXML_NAMESPACE_SXML now names only the sxml:token and sxml:node elements: no function is left in urn:sxml.

Errors ( default): tree-sitter:unknown-language and tree-sitter:invalid-query (), in the functions' namespace, as EXPath Binary 4.0 (1.5) and EXPath File 4.0 (1.7) put a module's errors in its functions' namespace. The description names the new functions ("the language is not one that tree-sitter:parse knows; tree-sitter:languages() lists them").
Elements stay in urn:sxml: sxml:token and sxml:node are sxml's mapping of a syntax tree, not tree-sitter's vocabulary, and keeping them keeps every document and tree-sitter/suite as they were.

Prefix bindings: sxml xpath and sxml xquery bind tree-sitter beside bin, file and sxml (apps/sxml/query_command.c); the JavaScript package binds it wherever the source-code feature is present (featurePrefixes in bindings/javascript/src/index.ts). The host shim binds no prefixes, and the Kotlin and Swift bindings (paused) do not bind sxml either. A stylesheet declares xmlns:tree-sitter="urn:sxml:tree-sitter" (); a library module declares it in its prolog.

For users (a breaking change, in CHANGELOG): replace sxml:parse-code with tree-sitter:parse, sxml:code-languages with tree-sitter:languages, Q{urn:sxml}parse-code with Q{urn:sxml:tree-sitter}parse, and catch tree-sitter:unknown-language instead of sxml:unknown-language; a stylesheet that declared xmlns:sxml for the function declares xmlns:tree-sitter.
Cost: two well-known namespace entries' worth of data, and one more binding per query in the CLI and the package; nothing per call.

Verified (): the debug preset (Clang, ASan, UBSan): source_code, name and the 258 CLI tests pass, tree-sitter/run-time-language passes; tree-sitter/suite 1,410 of 1,438 before and after; wasm preset javascript/code_languages and javascript/package pass; the book's affected chapters (source-code, call-chains, call-chains-graph, codegen-pipeline, codegen-typescript, ixml-performance, appendix-cli: 89 examples; javascript: 6) match.
